# FDG8002

> DO remember that arrays are mutable types—even arrays of immutable types.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.1 Arrays.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG8002
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

Message: Callers can change the elements of the read-only array field '{0}'

Test profile: test classes are public only for the test framework; their signatures are not API. FDG8002 reports an externally visible readonly field, static or instance, whose type is an array, as for Path.InvalidPathChars in the body: readonly protects the field, not the elements. A field initialized with an empty array is not reported: it has no elements to change (a constructor that assigns it a new array is not seen). Other ways of handing out an internal array (a method or property that returns it) are not seen, so coverage is partial; array properties are CA1819 (FDG8003). Replacing the field with a read-only collection or a method that returns a copy changes the public signature, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.

## From the book

It’s easy to fall into the logical fallacy that “one `Int32` is immutable, so `new Int32[] { 1, 2 }` is also immutable,” especially when it comes to the `readonly` field modifier. But the `readonly` field modifier only prevents replacing the entirety of the array; changing element values via the indexer is still possible.

This example demonstrates the pitfalls of using read-only array fields:

```csharp
//bad code
public sealed class Path {
  public static readonly char[] InvalidPathChars =
    { '\"', '<', '>', '|'};
}
```

This allows callers to change the values in the array as follows:

```csharp
Path.InvalidPathChars[0] = 'A';
```

Instead, you can either use a read-only collection (only if the items are immutable) or clone the array before returning it.

```csharp
public static ReadOnlyCollection<char> GetInvalidPathChars() {
  return Array.AsReadOnly(badChars);
}

public static char[] GetInvalidPathChars() {
  return (char[])badChars.Clone();
}
```

Another option available to immutable element types is `ReadOnlySpan<T>`. The Span types, and the trade-offs that come from them, are discussed in section 9.12.
